transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-20
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Diaz (OmniHealth - ML Ops), Maya Patel (OmniHealth - Security), Avery Chen (OmniHealth - PM)

Summary (auto): POC scoping call to align on data handling for a 4-week proof-of-concept. Key concerns: PII removal/redaction, logging and retention policy, whether prompts are stored and for how long, if prompt storage will be considered persistent PHI, and environment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC). Also discussed benchmark metrics and workload sizing.

00:00 Jordan: okay hi everyone thanks for joining, um let's do a quick roll call and then dive in. Jordan Lee here from Redwood, AE, gonna run the call.
00:12 Carlos: hey all, Carlos here, head of ML ops at OmniHealth. Thanks for setting this up.
00:18 Maya: Maya Patel, security. I'll be focusing on PII and compliance items.
00:22 Avery: Avery Chen, product. Interested in timelines and success criteria.
00:28 Priya: Priya Nair, SE at Redwood, I'll own the benchmark side and the redaction details.

01:05 Jordan: cool, the goal is to scope a 4-week POC where we run a small production-like workload to validate latency, cost, and data handling. We heard from your intake form that you have PHI-ish data, can you confirm?
01:20 Carlos: yes, we have patient notes and appointment transcripts. It's not all PHI all the time but some prompts include names and identifiers.
01:34 Maya: to be clear, anything that can be tied to a patient is PHI, so our bar is pretty strict. We'll need to know how Redwood handles redaction and retention.
01:44 Priya: understood. For the POC we can show you both a hosted flow with prompt-string redaction and a private deployment option. There are a few levers — on our hosted API we have logging levels, and you can opt out of data retention or enable automatic redaction. For private we can deploy into your VPC or on premise where logs never leave the customer network.
02:10 Carlos: when you say automatic redaction, what's persisted server-side? Are prompts stored in full in any logs, and for how long? Also curious about function-calls and KV cache — anything there that could persist PII?
02:26 Priya: good q. Short answer: by default hosted API stores logs for 30 days for debugging but you can request no-retention mode for the POC. Redaction can be at the API layer (we remove regex patterns, name entity recognition) before tokens hit storage. KV cache is in-memory on the runtime; it's not written to disk unless we explicitly snapshot for debugging. There can be artifacts in tracing if you enable tracing.
02:50 Maya: regex redaction is brittle for medical names. Do you do NER-based redaction? Is it configurable?
02:58 Priya: yes we support NER redaction (open-source models) and you can supply custom entity lists. It's a two-step pipeline: client-side token filtering + server-side NER. For high-assurance we recommend private deployment + client-side pre-filter for PHI removal.
03:18 Avery: for the POC success criteria we have a few asks: 95th percentile latency under 300ms for short prompts, sustain 50 RPS with 2k token windows, and no data persisted beyond the POC unless we opt in. Is that doable?
03:35 Priya: those are reasonable targets. We'll size the dedicated pool for 50 RPS. For 2k tokens we may need specific kernel/quantization settings; we'll run the benchmark.
03:46 Jordan: also we want to agree what counts as success for accuracy — you'll provide a small eval set or we can use your prompts to measure regression against your baseline.
03:55 Carlos: we'll supply a 500-prompt eval set and expected output quality bands.
04:02 Maya: what about logs for auditing? We do need audit logs showing who accessed the system, but logs should not contain raw prompts with PHI. We need a mechanism for redacted logs and an audit trail.
04:18 Priya: we can emit two-tier logs: metadata-only audit logs (user id, request id, timestamp, model/version) and redacted content logs where PII is masked. For on-prem or VPC, logs can be forwarded to your SIEM without leaving your network.
04:34 Carlos: can you demonstrate the masking process? I want to see false negatives — what slips through.
04:40 Priya: yes we'll include a masking test in the benchmark run; we'll run simulated transcripts with names, MRNs etc and show before/after. We'll log false-negative rate as part of the success criteria.
04:55 Maya: retention windows — what's configurable? 0 days, 7, 30? And is there immediate purge on request?
05:05 Priya: hosted supports configurable retention: no-retention (0 days non-persistent), 7, 30, 90. Immediate purge requested via API is supported but for hosted we do an internal retention job so there is a short propagation delay up to 24 hours for full purge. For dedicated/private the customer controls retention.
05:26 Carlos: how about backups or snapshotting? If you snapshot an instance with KV cache, could that include PII?
05:34 Priya: snapshots don't include in-memory KV unless debug snapshots are enabled; by default we don't persist KV cache in snapshots. We'll explicitly flag if we create any diagnostic snapshot.
05:46 Jordan: another ask from your legal — key management. Are keys customer-managed? KMS/HSM?
05:52 Priya: yes, we support BYOK and integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, and HSM for private). For hosted we encrypt at rest and in transit; for private we can use your KMS.
06:06 Maya: SOC2/ISO certifications? We need artifacts for procurement.
06:10 Jordan: we'll send our SOC2 Type II report and ISO attestations after the call. Also the security whitepaper that covers data flows and redaction.
06:18 Avery: timeline — we would like to start next Monday and run 4 weeks. Is that aggressive?
06:24 Priya: doable if we get sample traffic and an eval set this week. We need your QPS profile and sample prompts to configure the cluster and redaction rules.
06:34 Carlos: we can provide synthetic traffic and the eval set by Thursday. That would make the kickoff early next week.
06:40 Priya: perfect. Benchmark plan: week 0 kickoff + infra deploy, week 1 run baseline benchmarks (latency, p95/p99, RPS), week 2 run redaction tests and privacy checks, week 3 production-like run, week 4 wrap and handoff.
06:58 Carlos: for the benchmarks do you provide the harness or do we run it?
07:04 Priya: Redwood provides a harness (JMeter-based plus our load tool) and we'll share the scripts. You can also run from your env pointing to the secure endpoint. We'll coordinate.
07:14 Maya: one more — prompt storage concern: if a user sends a prompt that contains PHI, and you store prompts for debugging, is there any human access? Are there RBAC controls for who at Redwood can see logs?
07:28 Priya: good point. We have RBAC and logging for support access, with access approvals and audit trails. For hosted, support access to logs is gated; for private, we can disable support read access by default. We can also anonymize prompt content in support view.
07:44 Carlos: do you have a way to do deterministic redaction so output remains consistent for debugging? Sometimes masking changes output semantics.
07:50 Priya: we have token-level placeholders that preserve token count (e.g., [NAME_1]) to keep model context length similar. We document those transformations in an audit log.
08:05 Avery: can we keep a copy of raw prompts in a totally isolated S3 bucket under our account for debugging, so Redwood never sees raw?
08:12 Priya: yes, with private deployment or VPC we can set up S3 direct-forwarding into your account; Redwood wouldn't have keys to that bucket. That's the highest assurance option.
08:24 Maya: for POC probably start hosted no-retention + client-side pre-filter, then if results show any risk we'll move to private.
08:31 Jordan: that seems like a good path. We'll plan hosted no-retention for initial runs. Priya will design the benchmark and a masking test.
08:40 Priya: note on metrics: we'll capture p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, errors, and redaction false-neg rate. We'll also produce a cost estimate for 50 RPS at 2k tokens.
08:54 Carlos: cost estimate important for us. Also any throttling behavior you do at high concurrency? We need stable tail latencies.
09:02 Priya: we'll show autoscaling config and a steady-state run. We recommend pre-warming a dedicated pool for the POC to avoid cold-start jitters.
09:12 Jordan: Ok recapping next steps...
09:15 Jordan: Redwood to send SOC2/ISO docs, security whitepaper, and redaction checklist (action: Jordan by 2026-11-22).
09:23 Jordan: Priya to send benchmark plan + harness + masking test spec (action: Priya by 2026-11-24).
09:29 Jordan: Carlos to share sample traffic profile and the 500-prompt eval set (action: Carlos by 2026-11-23).
09:36 Maya: we'll review and if needed we'll request a private deployment quote.
09:40 Jordan: any other blockers?
09:43 Maya: just a question on legal — data processing addendum, we'll need DPIA outputs.
09:47 Jordan: we'll include DPA and DPIA template in the package.
09:50 Avery: sounds good, thanks everyone.
09:53 Jordan: thanks all. We'll follow up with the docs and propose a kickoff slot for next Monday at 14:00 UTC.

End of transcript
